title.narrative: Provision of integrated life-saving health services to the most vulnerable communities in under-served and hard-to-reach rural areas to address the impact of drought/AWD in Qansaxdhera district.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis URRO Health project is designed to address the critical health needs identified in in Qansaxdheere. The assessment by health cluster partners revealed that only 3% of the population currently has access to functional health services, with 71% of women in labor unable to reach healthcare facilities, resulting in tragic maternal deaths. Significant health challenges include a 97% prevalence of acute watery diarrhea, 58% of malaria, and 35% of respiratory infections, highlighting the urgent need for Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT) centres, routine immunizations, and expanded Outpatient Department (OPD) services. Vulnerable populations, including pregnant and lactating women, the elderly, and individuals with disabilities, will require targeted health interventions due to limited antenatal, delivery, and postnatal services and ineffective referral systems. This project will aim to strengthen maternal, neonatal, and child health services, improve access to routine vaccinations, enhance OPD and ORT services, and provide post-rape care through mobile and fixed health teams.Healthcare will be delivered at key locations in Qansax Dheere, including 3 fixed sites (Ahmed Gurey HC , Wadajir MHC, Busley HP) and two outreach teams in Korinbod, and October targeting 21,360 crisis-affected women, men, girls, and boys. The project will also ensure inclusive access by developing improved patient pathways and community outreach programs to remove barriers to healthcare for all genders and ages, ultimately aiming to save lives and significantly improve health outcomes for the most vulnerable populations in Qansax Dheereltbrgtlt/pgt
